## #211 — OWNER: Administration IA redesign approved; Phase 1 navigation regroup (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** The Owner approved the Administration redesign design package (Design canvas `https://claude.ai/artifact/KTgD1S6VrgGiyKNDxvUhto`, grounded in the 2026-10-08 UX review and the discovery brief `https://claude.ai/artifact/CR8GJ4Vce8UUTnnsP7jgKQ`) as presented, and authorized the UI-only phases 1–6. Settled: the 8-destination Administration IA; Page Layouts ships first as a read-only viewer (G1–G4 separate); Draft custom fields shown as they are today; Approval Requests under Roles. G6 (field-level access model) remains an open Owner decision; no UI-only phase depends on it.

Phase 1 (this entry) is presentation-only: `ADMINISTRATION_NAV_GROUPS` groups every configuration, communications, import and audit destination under **System & Integrations**; `ADMINISTRATION_NAV_ORDER` sets the rail's display order (Overview, Employees & Users, Objects, Roles, Workflows) without reordering the `administration` subnav array; Users → "Employees & Users" and Roles & Permissions → "Roles" are display-name changes only. No key, path, route, redirect, surface mapping, legacy gate, capability or server catalog changed, so the pinned production destination sets are byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Deferred, needs a decision:** the approved IA's separate **Permissions** destination is a new subnav key, which requires a `NAV_SURFACE_ACCESS` row (`administration/permissions` → the existing `administration.objects` surface) plus deliberate updates to the pinned destination counts (18 / 90 / 75 / 72). That row is a governance-map edit, so it was not made in Phase 1. Page Layouts' destination (Phase 5) has the same shape.

**Alternatives rejected:** reordering the subnav array to get Objects before Roles. It would have rewritten the pinned production b6a36b15 destination order for no behavioral gain.

## #212 — OWNER: Administration navigation authority for Permissions (and later Page Layouts) (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** The Owner approved the minimum `NAV_SURFACE_ACCESS` mappings for separate Administration destinations: **Permissions** reuses the existing `administration.objects` surface; **Page Layouts** may reuse the same authority as a read-only viewer. Navigation configuration only — no new capability, grant, role assignment or authorization mechanism.

This entry adds `administration/permissions` → `["administration.objects"]` and the `permissions` subnav item (no legacyKey, capabilityAccess or placeholder row). Consequences, stated rather than discovered:
- **Governed source:** Permissions opens exactly where Objects does, and for nobody else. App.jsx emits its route only on the same `isNavItemVisible` answer and a refusal route otherwise, so a direct URL is refused identically.
- **Legacy source** (every environment where `EOS_NAVIGATION_AUTHORITY_READY` is false, production included): Permissions is fail-closed for every role, like Rental (#207) and Analysis (#208). Opening it there would need a new legacy placeholder row, which this decision does not authorize. The matrix therefore stays reachable through Objects in those environments; Phase 2 must not remove it from Objects.
- **Pins moved on purpose:** Administration subnav 18 → 19; nav tree 90 → 91; the Administration container scope gains `administration/permissions` (it is a door onto a child surface). Legacy-visible sets (admin 75, dispatcher 72) are unchanged.
- Page Layouts' row lands with its read-only viewer (Phase 5), so no destination exists without a screen.

## #213 — Administration IA Phase 2: Objects opens with the object catalog (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** UI-only Phase 2 of the Owner-approved Administration redesign (#211). Where a policy store is configured, Administration → Objects now leads with the **Object catalog** (searchable by business name) and follows it with a **Permissions** section holding the same `ObjectAuthorityMatrix` and `ObjectActionSecurityPanel` it always mounted. A `?object=` deep link puts the Permissions section first, because it arrives to change permissions. The By Role / By Object toggle is no longer offered in that mode: both views rendered the same three components (review finding O02). The not-configured mode (code reference grid, role picker, By Object diagnostics) is unchanged.

Within the catalog: object and field keys sit behind **Show Technical Details** (O03); System fields read "System field" instead of "Protected"; a Reference custom field picks its target from the catalog by business name instead of a free-text object key, with the free-text input kept only if the catalog could not be read (O04); the field key is suggested from the label and stays editable; a successful create states that the field is a **Draft** that follows the object's access and does not yet store values or appear on a page (G5, G1).

**Why the matrix stays on Objects:** the separate Permissions destination (#212) is governed-source only, so in legacy-source environments Objects is the only door to the matrix.

**No backend change:** same reads (`listObjects`, `readObjectWithFields`) and commands (`updateObjectMetadata`, `createCustomField`, `updateCustomFieldMetadata`); the server validates the field key and requires a reference target to be named (it does not check that the target exists -- the picker only offers objects from the catalog).

## #214 — Administration IA Phase 3: Security Roles as a searchable master-detail (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** UI-only Phase 3 of the Owner-approved Administration redesign (#211).
- **Roles list (R01):** the wrapping wall of Role buttons becomes a searchable list (name and description) with an All / Protected / Not protected filter and a count, beside the selected Role's detail (`.fo-master-detail`, stacking under 900 px). Same `listRoles` read; the `?role=` deep link still pre-selects.
- **Role detail (R02):** `SecurityRoleDetail` opens on **Objects & Permissions**; **Employees** (holders, removal with reason, assign) and **History** (assignment history and decision history) are tabs. Every read, mutation, reason requirement and server refusal is unchanged.
- **Presentation (R03):** holder and Role keys sit behind *Show Technical Details*; "Since" and assignment-history times use the shared `formatDateOnly` / `formatTimestamp` instead of raw UTC strings; scope reads "Applies To".
- **Kept distinct, not redesigned:** a one-line explainer separates Security Role (what someone may do), Job Role (what their job is; grants nothing) and permission (one enforced action). No authority model changed.

Out of scope and not attempted: resolving "By" actor ids to names in assignment history (needs a read the screen does not have today).

## #215 — Administration IA Phase 4: Permissions reads as access, then business actions (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** UI-only Phase 4 of the Owner-approved Administration redesign (#211), in the shared permission matrix (`ObjectAuthorityMatrix`, rendered on Objects and on Permissions) and the per-cell grant controls.

- **Bands and order (P01):** columns are ordered Create, Read, Edit, Delete, then business actions, then administration actions, under *Object Access* / *Business Actions* / *Administration* band headings. Ordering is stable within a kind; the grid's cell indexes, bulk plans and every mutation are unchanged.
- **Unavailable verbs are shown, not omitted (P02):** for each of Create / Read / Edit / Delete an Object has no action for, the matrix shows a column marked *Not Available* with the reason "EOS has no Delete action for Work Orders". It is never a control, never part of a bulk plan, and invents no grant.
- **No dead condition form (P03):** when the server's condition vocabulary has answered and no kind applies to the capability, *Set Condition* is disabled with "No supported conditions for this action." While the vocabulary is loading or unavailable the opener stays and the form explains why, as before; an active condition can still be replaced or retired.

Not changed: state words (Granted / Granted (Conditional) / Not Granted / Not Available), capability keys behind the column legend, server enforcement. G6 (field-level access) remains an open Owner decision and is not represented as configurable.

Restricted to Administration; no other workspace, no global visual change, no backend, permission, role-grant, identity, schema or workflow-engine change, no Firebase, no production deploy.

## #217 — Administration UI corrections PR 2: Roles (ADMIN-UI-005, 006, 007) (2026-10-09)

**Decision:** Part 2 of the Owner-approved corrections (#216), Administration → Roles only, styled under `.fo-admin`.
- **005:** full-width search with an icon inside the list panel (consistent height, focus ring), a compact segmented All / Protected / Not protected filter (`aria-pressed`), and an unobtrusive "n of N" count. Search and filter behavior and protected-role semantics are unchanged.
- **006:** the Role list is a compact, scrollable list of full-width rows with dividers, a clear selected state (`aria-pressed`, `aria-current`) and keyboard focus, and a small *Protected* badge -- replacing outlined buttons. Selecting the selected Role again keeps it selected.

Rule, all over the Roles `listRoles` already returned (nothing widens visibility): an explicit choice wins while it still matches the search and filter, otherwise the first matching Role is shown; a `?role=` link selects that Role; **if the link names a Role that is not in the list, the panel says "The linked Security Role isn't available" and substitutes nothing** until the administrator chooses (Owner safeguard); when nothing matches, an explicit empty state is shown.
- **Edit Role Details is bound to one Role** (independent review, blocking): because the shown Role can now change with the search and filter, the editor is open only while the Role it was opened for is the one shown, and the form is keyed by that Role. A changed selection closes it, so a save can never write one Role's draft to another.

## #219 — OWNER: separate Workflow Assignments from Workflow Builder (2026-10-08)

**Decision:** Rudy approved Workflow Assignments as the main Administration workflow page and Workflow Builder as a separate linked page. Assignment work shows action-to-Security-Role associations and role holders. Definition authoring, validation diagnostics, version lifecycle, activation and migration stay in Builder. The previous recommendation to treat the main page as a builder with tabs is superseded.

**Implementation boundary:** existing authorization and immutable published-version behavior are retained. Role-only edits are validated and saved as a new inactive draft; publication remains a Builder operation. No new capability, grant, server policy, Firebase dependency, migration or live configuration change. Existing route/access gate is shared through distinct page URLs (`?view=builder`); the query selects presentation only.

**Evidence:** `docs/testing/workflow-assignments-ux-correction.md`; user guide `docs/user-guide/administration/workflow-assignments.md`. Local implementation is not live acceptance or deployment authority.

## #220 — OWNER: W01 foundation D2 and D3 — the caller's own workflow decisions; eligible Roles from validation (2026-10-09)

**Decision:** Rudy approved D2 and D3 only. D1, replacing the global router so that in-app Back can be blocked while there are unsaved changes, needs its own Owner decision and is not part of this change.
- **D2:** a new read-only Administration read, `readMyWorkflowAdministration`. It is gated on `workflowDefinition.read`, the same gate as `listWorkflows`, and takes no input, so a caller can only ask about itself.
  - It answers each workflow mutation the API serves with `{ allowed, requiredCapability, requiredLabel }`.
  - The answer comes from `decideWorkflowMutation`, the same function every mutation enforces with, so the two cannot differ.
  - Workflow Builder and Workflow Assignments offer a mutation only when it is allowed. Otherwise they say why, and they fail closed while the answer is unknown or unreadable.
  - Server enforcement is unchanged.
- **D3:** `readWorkflowVersion` additionally returns `actions[].eligibleRoles` and `roleNames`.
  - The eligible Roles are those that hold the action's capability. They come from `loadWorkflowValidationContext`, the map `BINDING_WITHOUT_CAPABILITY` uses, so an eligible Role is exactly one that validation accepts.
  - `eligibleRoles` is `null` when the action names no capability or an unknown one.
  - Workflow Assignments offers only eligible Roles and no longer needs `admin.securityPolicy.read`.
  - Existing bindings that conflict with eligibility are shown and explained, never removed automatically.
  - Disclosure is limited to the key and name of the Roles holding the capabilities a readable workflow names.

**Boundary:** no capability, grant, Role, migration, workflow definition or mapping change, and no Firebase dependency. The role-holder lookup for Workflow Assignments is designed separately and is not implemented without its own approval.

## #221 — OWNER: W01 holder lookup `listWorkflowActionRoleHolders` (2026-10-09)

**Decision:** Rudy approved a narrow, read-only lookup that lists the Employees holding one Security Role relevant to one workflow action. Workflow Assignments' "View employees" now uses it instead of the Security Role detail, which needs the whole Security Policy read.

**Who may call it:**
- The caller needs `workflowDefinition.read`, the surface gate, AND either `workflowDefinition.edit` or `workflowDefinition.version`, the save an assignment makes. Both are decided by `decideWorkflowMutation`.
- Otherwise it refuses with `WORKFLOW_ASSIGNMENT_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`.

**What it answers:**
- **Tenant:** the caller's tenant only. Another tenant's version returns NOT_FOUND.
- **Roles:** only a Role that is eligible for the action (holds its capability) or already bound to it. Any other Role is refused with `ROLE_NOT_FOR_ACTION`.
- **Holders:** one entry per person the runtime would let act at all. That means an active principal with an active tenant membership whose linked Employee (if any) is access-eligible, holding the Role through an active, non-stale assignment. Suspended principals, inactive memberships and terminated Employees are not holders. This fix came from independent review.
- **appliesToAction:** true only when the Role is eligible, its grant carries no active condition, and the assignment is global or has a scope that decides the action's capability. When false, `notApplicableReason` says why: `ROLE_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `CONDITIONED_GRANT` or `SCOPE_DOES_NOT_DECIDE`.
- **Counts (OWNER RULING, 2026-10-09):** headcount disclosure across Employee-visibility boundaries is **rejected**. `totalHolders`, `holdersForAction` and `truncated` are computed only over the holders the caller may view as Employees, the same set the names come from. There is no `withheld` count. A caller with no Employee visibility receives zero counts and no names. Counts are per person, not per assignment.
- **Employee names:** shown only where the existing Employee visibility admits them. This is the Workforce read kernel's `employee.record.read` check, applied per operating company for scoped holders, and injected by the server (`eosAdministration/workflowHolderVisibility.ts`).
  - Holders outside that visibility, or not linked to an Employee, are neither named nor counted.
  - If visibility cannot be established, the lookup refuses with `EMPLOYEE_VISIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE`. It never returns an empty list in that case. An unavailable context authority also counts as visibility that cannot be established.
- **Fields returned:** Role key and name, `roleEligible` and `roleBound`, `totalHolders`, `holdersForAction`, `employeeVisibility` (about the caller only), `truncated`, and up to 200 holders. Each holder has a display name, an Employee id (used only for the record link), its scope, `appliesToAction` and `notApplicableReason`.
- **Never returned:** principal ids, sign-in identities, other Roles or capabilities.

**Boundary:** read-only; grants nothing. No capability, grant, Role, migration, workflow definition or mapping change, and no Firebase dependency.

## #222 — OWNER: the Administrator has full EOS access, including operational reach — Reorder queue (2026-10-09)

(Follows #219–#221, recorded by PR #2035.)

**Defect.** For the Administrator, the Inventory & Supply Overview showed only "Failed to load: reading the Reorder queue requires the REORDER_QUEUE Operational Scope".

**Root cause.** The queue read requires the capability `reorder.request.read` AND a REORDER_QUEUE Operational Scope, which is company-keyed and held by the caller's linked Employee (`reorderLifecycleCommands.requireQueueReach`).
- The Administrator holds the capability, because `admin` derives the full catalog (Owner ruling 2026-08-19).
- Operational Scope is a separate, per-Employee dimension (workforce rulings 2026-09-17). The full-access ruling never extended to it.
- The Administrator's Employee did hold `REORDER_QUEUE:taylor`, seeded by migration 1761696000000. That scope was marked "proposed: withdraw" in the persona-needs fixture.
- The 2026-10-03 Taylor workforce manifest then rebuilt the Employee with `scopes: []`.
- Separately, the Overview loaded its panels with an unsettled `Promise.all`. The one refused read replaced the whole page.

**Decision.** The Administrator has full EOS access including operational reach, through the existing model and with no code bypass.
- The Administrator's Employee holds REORDER_QUEUE for every keyed company. Today that is `taylor` only. Nonprod Ventana is unkeyed (see the Finance closure record), and the governed writer refuses an unkeyed queue (`REORDER_QUEUE_NOT_FOUND`), so `REORDER_QUEUE:ventana` follows once Ventana's company key is bound. Binding it is a separate configuration ruling. Independent review caught this.
- The scope is issued through the governed Workforce writer (`assignEmployeeOperationalScope`) by a different authorized principal, the Owner persona. Self-scoping stays refused (`OPERATIONAL_SCOPE_SELF`).
- The Overview now settles the purchase-order read, as it already did for the Work Order aggregates. A refusal is stated inside the Procurement panel and no longer blanks the other panels.

**Not included; needs separate Owner decisions.**
- **WAREHOUSE scopes** (decision item #2038). These are per-warehouse read reach for on-hand, receipts, warehouses, transfers and warehouse measures. They would also open `warehouse.management` and `warehouse.picking`, which the P02 persona record lists as must-not-reach.
- **Any Work Eligibility.** `ADMIN_IMPLIES_NO_WORK_ELIGIBILITY` stands. Eligibility would make the Administrator a dispatchable technician or warehouse worker, and would open cycle-count work.

**Boundary.**
- No capability, grant, Role, migration, policy model or Firebase change.
- Production is not altered. The Administrator's scopes in any environment are issued through Administration → Employee → Operational Scope by the Owner (or another administrator), or in nonprod by the reviewed workforce seed.

## #223 — OWNER: the protected Administrator holds full company system authority by STANDING — PR-1 (2026-10-09)

**Ruling (Owner, final, 2026-10-09).**
- **Owner:** ultimate company governance. Appoints the initial Administrator, appoints and revokes Administrators, and keeps protected ownership. An Administrator never removes or overrides the Owner.
- **Administrator:** the company's system controller, through the existing designated protected `admin` Role. There is no new Role and no parallel system.
  - Full company-scoped system authority, resolved centrally on the server. A new system-administration capability is covered with no grant.
  - Appoints and revokes OTHER Administrators. There is one tier.
  - Not a job assignment: no Work Eligibility, no record assignment, no MOBILE scope. Worker-only acts keep their requirements.
- **Operational employees and managers:** receive capabilities, scopes and assignments by job. They never get Administrator authority by implication.

**Standing** (`functions/src/adminPolicy/protectedAdministrator.ts`). The principal context has already established an authenticated, enabled principal, an active membership and tenant, and employment eligibility. On top of that, standing requires:
- an active GLOBAL assignment of the Role whose key is `admin` AND whose stored `protected` flag is set;
- NOT also holding the protected Owner Role. Owner and Administrator stay distinct authority types.

**What standing implies.**
- **Implied:** every `ADMIN_ACTION` and every `READ` capability, plus every action on a system-administration Object: `rolesPermissions`, `workflowDefinition`, `principal`, `employee`, `auditLog`, `dataImport`, `systemConfiguration`, `financeConfiguration`.
- **Excluded:** `reorder.request.read.queue` (superseded) and `salesAgreement.tradeIn.approve` (Owner/GM).
- **Not implied (O1):** `BUSINESS_ACTION`, `CREATE` and `EDIT` on business Objects. Business approval, financial execution and operational execution keep their existing authorization until a capability-by-capability classification is approved.
- **Existing grants (O3):** retained. Standing adds; it removes nothing.

**Where it is resolved.** The three root resolvers:
- `capabilityAuthority.resolveOperationalCapabilities`: the flat set, the entitled seam and `capabilitiesWithoutUnevaluatedConditions`;
- `administrationCapabilityGate.capabilityKeysFor`;
- `adminPolicyApi.resolvePrincipalEffectiveAccess`.

Implied keys are unconditioned and carry the provenance `PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR` in Effective Access.

**Delegation.**
- The Owner appoints and removes through R1.
- An Administrator with standing appoints and removes OTHER Administrators: global only, re-verified against the store under the governance lock.
- Self-appointment and self-removal are refused (`SELF_ADMINISTRATION`).
- The last Administrator is never removed. The anti-lockout count stays grant-row based, which is stricter.
- The protected Owner is never appointed or removed through ordinary role administration.
- The Administrator Role is refused to a principal holding the protected Owner (`PROTECTED_ROLE_CONFLICT`). Historical memberships are not altered.

**Audit.** Every Administration write by an actor with standing records `after.authorizedBy = { standing: "PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR", ruling }`. This covers policy, workflow, workflow lifecycle and instances, and Employee administration through the Workforce kernel. An R1 staffing record keeps its own `authorizedBy`. Audit stays append-only.

**Superseded.**
- The principle "holding `admin` is not a substitute for the capability" (`administrationAuthority.ts`), and its bootstrap note in `workflowAdministration.ts`.
- R2 ("no self-bootstrap exception") for the Administrator. R2 still describes how every OTHER Role gets workflow authority.
- R1 as Owner-only staffing: protected Administrators also staff Administrators.
- DQ-210-A is resolved by the system / approval / execution distinction above.

**Approved but NOT in PR-1.**
- Company-wide WAREHOUSE and REORDER_QUEUE administration reach without an Employee scope, with worker execution preserved (D3; PR-2).
- Domain-writer audit consistency (PR-3).
- The O1 classification (PR-4).
- Cleanup after acceptance (PR-5).

**Boundary.**
- No new capability, no grant written or removed, no migration, no Firebase.
- Production: a read-only Owner/Administrator dual-membership census is required before activation (O4).

## #224 — OWNER: protected Administrator ADMINISTRATION REACH over Reorder queues and warehouses — PR-2 (2026-10-09)

(Follows #223, PR-1. Implements #223 D3 and G2.)

**Ruling (Owner, 2026-10-09).** A protected Administrator administers company-scoped operational configuration without an Employee Operational Scope or a worker assignment. This is administration REACH, never operational execution.

**Reach** (`functions/src/eosOps/administrationReach.ts`). The only way in is PR-1 standing, re-read from the store by the same rule (`principalHasProtectedAdministratorStanding`): an enabled principal, an active membership, active global non-stale assignments, no ineligible linked Employee, the protected `admin` Role, and no Owner.
- **REORDER_QUEUE:** every company key bound ACTIVE, in this tenant, to an ACTIVE operating company.
- **WAREHOUSE:** every ACTIVE warehouse of such a company.
- **Never reached:** another tenant, an INACTIVE warehouse, an unbound or INACTIVE company key.

**Consumers.**
- **Read reach:**
  - `reorderQueueReach.queueReachKeys` is now the ONE queue reach. It replaces the copies in the Reorder lifecycle and assignment modules, and is used by My Work search, analysis and assigned-work reads.
  - `partsReads.scopedWarehouseIds` covers on-hand, receipts, movements, transfers, truck stock and warehouse analysis.
  - The receiving-location picker opts OUT: it offers only where the caller can receive.
- **Predicate reach:** `contextualAuthorization`'s `OPERATIONAL_SCOPE` predicate admits standing only when ALL of these hold:
  - the call site opts in (`administrationReach`);
  - the capability is on the allow-list (`warehouse.record.read`, `reorder.request.read`, `inventory.receipt.correct`);
  - the scope type is REORDER_QUEUE or WAREHOUSE (never MOBILE).

  Call sites that opt in: the experience surfaces (inspection) and the receipt correction for `VOID` only (G2 reversal). A source-scan test pins exactly these.

**Never execution.**
- The 10 O1 WORKER capabilities and `inventory.stock.receive` are an explicit exclusion set, disjoint from the allow-list.
- The receipt CORRECTED path re-receives through the receive pipeline, whose `inventory.stock.receive` WAREHOUSE gate no call site opts in, so re-receiving stays the worker's own authority.
- MOBILE scope is never reached.
- Purchasing steps are assignee-gated and never consult reach.
- WORK_ELIGIBILITY and RECORD_ASSIGNMENT predicates are untouched.

Management decisions that reach enables (review, cancel, void, assign) still require their OWN capability, which arrives with PR-4.

**Boundary.**
- Employee scopes and grants are retained, including the Administrator Employee's historical `REORDER_QUEUE:taylor`.
- No migration, no new capability, no grant, no Firebase.
- Business-state validation and append-only audit are unchanged.

## #225 — Protected Administrator AUDIT PROVENANCE in every direct audit writer — PR-3 (2026-10-10)

(Follows #223 D7 and #224. Implements the Owner's "Administrator authorization provenance must be recorded consistently".)

PR-1 stamped the Administration repository and the Workforce kernel. PR-3 stamps every OTHER direct writer of `eos_policy.audit_events`:
- configuration: system, finance, warehouse/bin, truck registry, scope binding, supplier, sales discount;
- catalog;
- purchasing, reorder lifecycle and assignment;
- inventory receive, correction, placement, relocation, transfer, cycle count, acquire;
- rental and billing;
- scheduling and self-scheduling;
- inbound work;
- the Workforce Job Role and Functional Role catalogs;
- preview-as-user.

That is 29 writers in 28 files, all through ONE helper, `administrationReach.withActorAuthority`. It applies the same standing rule as reach and stamps `after.authorizedBy` only when the acting principal has standing. It never overwrites an existing `authorizedBy` and leaves non-record payloads unchanged.

Operator migration, cutover and copy tooling and fixtures have no acting principal with standing. They are listed as exempt.

A source-scan test fails if any non-exempt direct writer stops using the helper.

**Boundary.** No migration, no capability, no grant. Audit stays append-only. The cost is one indexed read per stamped write.

## #226 — Trade-in approval RESERVED to Owner / General Manager (SYSTEM_INVARIANT) — PR-4a (2026-10-10)

(Implements Owner ruling G7, 2026-10-09. Amends nothing in #204: its grants were already owner / generalManager only.)

`salesAgreement.tradeIn.approve` is a **RESERVED capability**. `roleCapabilityAdministration.RESERVED_CAPABILITY_HOLDERS` is an allow-list naming the only Roles that may hold it: `owner` and `generalManager`.

**Grant side.** `forbiddenPair` treats every other Role as a forbidden OWNER_GOVERNANCE pair, whether built-in or custom, existing or future. The one precedence rule therefore:
- refuses the grant (`SYSTEM_INVARIANT`);
- makes every default writer skip it;
- shows the Administration grant matrix cell as an invariant;
- reports a stored row as `FORBIDDEN_PRESENT`.

A direct Principal grant of a reserved capability is refused outright. Verification reports such a holding as `FORBIDDEN_PRINCIPAL_HOLDING`.

**Effective side.** The trade-in decision (approve and decline) and the Commercial client offer additionally require the actor to hold a reserved Role through a qualifying global assignment. This is the same qualifying rule that standing uses (`administrationReach.qualifyingGlobalRoles`). A grant that predates the invariant therefore decides nothing (`RESERVED_CAPABILITY`, FORBIDDEN). Protected Administrator standing still never implies the capability (#223).

**Census before change (nonprod, read-only, 2026-10-10).** Holders by grant are `owner` and `generalManager` only, through 3 principals, all synthetic fixtures. There were 0 conflicts. Nothing was revoked, and nothing is revoked automatically.

**Boundary.** No migration, capability or grant change.

Because self-scoping is refused (`OPERATIONAL_SCOPE_SELF`), the workforce seed issued the Administrator's scopes as the Owner persona. #224 now gives the protected Administrator company-wide REORDER_QUEUE and WAREHOUSE administration reach by STANDING (`functions/src/eosOps/administrationReach.ts`, `reorderQueueReach.ts`). ## #229 — OWNER: security-relevant authorization denials are audited, rate-bounded and privacy-preserving (2026-10-11)

(Adopted by the Owner in the Firebase Equivalence Remediation package, Phase 3. Resolves finding AUD-1 of the Firebase retirement equivalence audit, `docs/audits/firebase-retirement-equivalence-2026-10-11/README.md`.)

**Context.**
- The Firestore-era enterprise-access specification (§5.8 outcome `applied | denied`, §14) required denied attempts to be audited. The Firebase commands did so (`requireCapabilityOrAudit`, `trustedWriterCommands.ts:549`).
- No PostgreSQL-era decision required or waived it. Every EOS domain refused without an audit row: catalog, supplier, workforce, Administration policy, operations and CRM.
- An auditor could not reconstruct attempted unauthorized actions, including attempted role-grant and employee-change actions.

**Decision (EOS-wide policy).**
1. **Security-relevant authorization denials are recorded** in the governed audit trail (`eos_policy.audit_events`). A denial is an operation refused to a **resolved** EOS Principal by an authorization rule: a missing capability, a non-member or inactive Principal, or a scope or eligibility refusal. Validation, not-found, conflict and precondition answers are business answers, not denials.
2. **What a row records:** the Principal, the tenant, the operation, the required capability, the refusal code, the timestamp, and a correlation identifier when the request carried a well-formed one.
3. **What a row never records:** a request payload, a credential or token, or a caller-stated identifier that was not resolved. An unresolved identity is not recorded under a caller-stated tenant, because that would let any caller write into any tenant's log.
4. **Rate-bounded:** at most one row per (tenant, Principal, operation, refusal code, minute). The trail is append-only, so it must not be growable without bound.
5. **Fail-safe:** a failure to write the audit row never changes the outcome. The operation stays denied, and the failure is logged without payload.
6. **Review before activation:** any change to the database schema or to the audit-event contract is reviewed before it is activated in an environment.

**Implementation (separate draft PR, not active).**
- Shared server support is `functions/src/eosAudit/authorizationDenialAudit.ts`. It needs no schema change. Each row is one `audit_events` row with action `<domain>.<operation>.denied`, target kind `authorization` and a deterministic per-minute id with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- The first adopter is the Catalog transport (write and read refusals).
- The helper ships with mode **OFF**. Activating it, and adopting it in the other domains, are reviewed changes.

**Boundary.** No grant, capability, Role or authority change. Authorization outcomes are unchanged. No Firebase.

## #230 — OWNER: governed field groups are the EOS Core field-permission mechanism (2026-10-12)

(Owner direction of 2026-10-12, on SUP-1 Part Supplier Terms, PR #2064. Mechanism: `docs/architecture/governed-field-groups.md`.)

**Decision (as directed by the Owner).**
1. **Mechanism.** Governed field groups are the reusable EOS Core field-permission mechanism. `role_field_permission_overrides` and the retired field-override UI are **not** revived.
2. **Explicit commercial capabilities.** Commercial READ, CREATE and EDIT each use an explicit capability: `inventory.catalog.cost.read`, `.create` and `.edit`.
3. **Standing exclusion.** Commercial capabilities are excluded from protected Administrator standing (`PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR_EXCLUSIONS`).
4. **No title inference.** Cost access is not inferred from the Owner, Administrator, General Manager, Parts Manager or Warehouse Manager titles.
5. **Narrow supplier-terms record capability.** Supplier terms get a narrow record capability: `inventory.supplierTerms.read`, `.create`, `.edit` and `.changeStatus` on `supplierCatalogItem`. Broad `inventory.catalog.manage` is not granted merely so that a Purchasing Manager can maintain supplier terms, and supplier terms no longer depend on `inventory.catalog.manage` or `inventory.catalog.activate`.
6. **Proposed grants.** Grants are **proposed** for Purchasing Manager and Inventory Catalog Administrator (see the doc, §6.1). They are **not executed**. Executing them needs further Owner authorization.
7. **Objects matrix.** The Administration Objects matrix represents the new capabilities and the field-group actions accurately.
8. **Audit and disclosure.**
   - Append-only audit integrity is preserved.
   - Supplier costs are not exposed through general audit reads, reporting, replay outcomes or response echoes.
   - The version-change metadata disclosure is documented as accepted: a version bump, or an audit reason naming a changed field, reveals *that* a restricted field changed, never its value.

**Implementation (PR #2064, unmerged).**
- Migration `1764530000000_supplier-terms-capabilities.sql` registers the seven keys with **zero grants** and a guarded Down.
- The COMMERCIAL fields are `reportable: false`.
- The Administrator's standing implies `inventory.supplierTerms.read` only (a READ, #223). Create, edit and changeStatus are not implied.

**Boundary.**
- No grant, Role or persona change.
- No nonprod or production data touched.
- No Firebase.

## #231 — OWNER: Return intake is a temporary, documented gap while Warehouse Scan moves to EOS capabilities (D-SCAN-2 Option A, 2026-10-13)

(Owner checkpoint of 2026-10-13 on UAT P1-2 / PR #2083. D-SCAN-1 = B moved all three Scan mounts from the legacy Firebase capability feed to EOS `resolveMyCapabilities`.)

**Decision (as directed by the Owner).**
1. **Option A.** The Scan workflow "Take a return in" (Return intake) is not offered by EOS until its command moves to EOS.
   - No Firebase fallback is kept for it.
   - No capability, grant or migration is created for it.
2. **Truthful state.** The workflow is listed as unavailable with the reason `NOT_YET_IN_EOS`: "Taking a return in is not yet available in EOS". It is never shown as a missing permission ("not authorized … an administrator can grant it"), because nobody can grant it.
3. **Authorization unchanged.** The workflow's capability check (`inventory.returns.intake`) and every other warehouse authorization and scope check are unchanged.

**The gap, precisely.**
- **What becomes unavailable.**
  - Only the Scan entry point to Return intake: `ReturnIntakeScan`, reached through `ScanWorkspace` from `/service/scan`, the warehouse handheld (its Home "Returns" queue) and the technician shell. It called the Firebase callable `recordReturnIntake` (`functions/src/inventoryReturns/returnCallables.ts`).
  - The callable writes one Firestore `inventory_returns` record in state `AWAITING_DISPOSITION`. It makes no ledger, balance or serialized-asset change, and records no disposition. Disposition does not exist (#118).
  - Under the Firebase feed, the key is activated for eos-platform-sandbox (`config/environments.json`). Two kinds of principal could reach it:
    - the Firebase administrator, who holds the whole catalog;
    - principals holding the `inventoryReturnsIntakeClerk` Role in the sandbox: the certification-world fixtures `cw-emp-029` and `cw-emp-044` (`docs/governance/certification-grant-manifest.json`) and the warehouse-manager persona fixture (`personaOperability.test.mjs`).
  - All of them lose the Scan entry point. None of them is real Taylor workforce.
- **No EOS equivalent exists.**
  - Rental return (`rentalEquipment.return`) covers rental fleet units only.
  - Transfers and stock relocation move stock internally.
  - The PostgreSQL movement type `RETURNED` has no writer.
- **Operational impact: none blocking.**
  - Intake has no stock effect, and Firebase data is SAMPLE (Owner ruling, 2026-10-01).
  - No work order, parts or rental process depends on it.
  - Its only acceptance check (V-12, scanner sandbox promotion 2026-08-20) was never run.
- **Not removed.** The callable stays deployed and exported, so the capability-equivalence guard is unaffected. When `recordReturnIntake` is eventually removed, its equivalence record must cite this decision as an accepted GAP.

**Known narrow residue (not changed).** A browser tab that had Return intake open before this change can reopen it from session storage (`eos.scan.activeWorkflow`). `rememberedWorkflow()` checks only that the stored value is a known workflow name, not that the workflow is available.
- For a principal the Firebase callable still authorizes (above), a submission from such a tab still succeeds and writes the SAMPLE `inventory_returns` record.
- This existed before #2083 and ends when the callable is retired.

**Boundary.**
- Client only: `field-ops-app-vite/src/access/scanWorkflows.js`.
- No server, grant, capability, migration, Firebase or production change.

## #232 — OWNER: Financial Policy authority amendment and the PostgreSQL foundation — Finance prepares, Owner / Administrator approve and activate (2026-10-13)

(Owner direction of 2026-10-13: implement the EXISTING CERT-FIN-02 accounting-policy-profile architecture in PostgreSQL. It continues the Owner ruling of 2026-09-03 and its §7 lifecycle (`docs/assessments/cert-fin-02-policy-framework-reconciliation.md`); it is not a redesign. Authority matrix: `docs/financials/financial-policy-foundation-authority.md`.)

**Supersedes.** This decision SUPERSEDES the holder portion of the earlier financial-policy authority ruling, commit `5b2bb0c6` (PR #1778): "`financialPolicy.profile.configure` is held by admin and owner ONLY, by derivation". From this decision:
- configuration (preparing, editing and submitting a policy) belongs to Finance Manager and Controller, not to admin and owner;
- admin and owner approve, reject and activate.

The rest of that ruling stands:
- read authority never implies write;
- no capability, including admin's and owner's, edits a locked policy;
- production activation is a separate ruling.

The Firebase catalog ids `financialPolicy.profile.read` / `.configure`, their sandbox activation and `financialPolicyProfileCommand.ts` are NOT changed (Firebase is retirement-only).

**Decision (as directed by the Owner).**
1. **Prepare.** Finance Manager and Controller may configure, edit drafts and submit Financial Policies.
2. **Decide and activate.** Owner and Administrator may approve, reject and activate Financial Policies.
3. **Separation of duties.** A preparer cannot approve their own submission. As implemented, the principal who approves OR rejects is neither the submitter nor any principal who wrote the draft's content, even when that principal holds the approve capability.
4. **Independent companies.** Taylor and Ventana maintain independent policies.
5. **Lock.** Activated policy versions are locked.
6. **Revision.** Future changes require governed revision and approval: a new version through the same lifecycle. There is no unlock, reopen or force path.

**Implementation (this PR, unmerged).**
- **Migration `1764560000000_financial-policy-profiles.sql`.** It creates `eos_finance.financial_policy_versions`, keyed by (tenant, operating company) against `eos_policy.tenant_operating_companies`, never CONSOLIDATED. It has a guarded Down.
- **Lifecycle.** DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> APPROVED or REJECTED; APPROVED -> ACTIVE; ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED.
  - Content is frozen once a version leaves DRAFT. Lifecycle stamps are write-once. Nothing is deleted.
  - An ACTIVE row admits only its supersession by the activation of a later approved version of the same company, in the same transaction (a deferred check).
  - REJECTED and SUPERSEDED are final.
  - At most one ACTIVE and one in-flight version per company (partial unique indexes).
  - Database triggers and CHECKs enforce all of the above, including separation of duties. In addition:
    - TRUNCATE is refused by a statement trigger;
    - even in DRAFT, `content_authors` only grows and `prepared_by` never changes.
  - A CHECK refusal that a racing write reaches answers as a governed refusal (for example `SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES`, 403), never a 500.
- **Effective date at ACTIVATION, not approval.** An approval may wait; a date fixed earlier could lapse, leaving an approved version that can neither activate nor be edited. The date may not precede the company's business date (`eos_policy.operating_company_business_date`) nor an earlier activated version's.
- **Lifecycle is not effectivity.** Activation locks a version and supersedes the prior ACTIVE one at once, but a version governs only from its own effective date.
  - The version IN FORCE on a business date is the latest ACTIVE or SUPERSEDED version whose effective date is on or before it. A SUPERSEDED row keeps its own effective date.
  - A future-dated ACTIVE version is reported as SCHEDULED, not in force.
  - `readFinancialPolicy` returns `inForce` (or `NOT_CONFIGURED`), `scheduled` and the version in flight. It accepts an `asOfDate`.
- **Missing policy fails closed.** A company with no version in force reads `NOT_CONFIGURED`, including when its first-ever activation is still scheduled. No default method exists anywhere.
- **Validation** is the pure domain module `functions/src/finance/financialPolicyProfile.ts`, imported unchanged. LIFO and STANDARD are refused, and `WORK_ORDER_CONSUMPTION` follows `PHYSICAL_CONSUMPTION_ACTIVE`. It is re-checked at submit, approval and activation.
- **Server.** `functions/src/eosFinance/financialPolicy.ts`, on `/operations/finance`. Every state change writes one `eos_policy.audit_events` row carrying the full version snapshot, from which the history rebuilds.
- **Replay.** An identical re-sent command writes nothing and answers `replayed: true`. A re-send whose effect is recorded but whose reason or note differs is refused with `FINANCIAL_POLICY_REPLAY_CONFLICT` (409), so a note is never silently dropped.
- **Capabilities.** Four PG-native keys on the new `financialPolicy` Object, with **zero grants**. The Firebase ids are deliberately not reused, to avoid the catalog reconcile granting them to admin.

  | Key | Kind | Operations |
  |---|---|---|
  | `finance.policy.read` | READ | read the policy, list versions |
  | `finance.policy.prepare` | EDIT | save a draft, submit |
  | `finance.policy.approve` | ADMIN_ACTION | approve, reject |
  | `finance.policy.activate` | ADMIN_ACTION | activate |

- **The Administrator, by standing (#223).** Protected-Administrator standing implies READ and ADMIN_ACTION kinds. So the Administrator holds `finance.policy.read`, `.approve` and `.activate` **without a grant**, and does NOT hold `.prepare` (EDIT is not implied). No `PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR_EXCLUSIONS` entry is needed. This is exactly item 2 for the Administrator. The audit trail marks standing-authorized acts `PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR`.
- **Proposed grants: SUPERSEDED by #232 Phase 1 (below).** This PR originally proposed:
  - `financeManager` and `controller`: `finance.policy.read` + `.prepare`;
  - `owner`: `finance.policy.read` + `.approve` + `.activate`.

  Phase 1 replaces those proposals. The existing finance Roles stay unchanged.
  - No Sales, Service, Parts or Warehouse Role, and neither `accountingManager` nor `generalManager`, is proposed anything.

**Open Owner decisions (recorded, not built).**
1. **Scheduled corrections.** While a future-dated version is scheduled, a correction must be dated AFTER it: effective dates strictly increase and no cancel-scheduled path exists. Should a governed "cancel scheduled activation" exist?
2. ~~**Company scope is data-only.**~~ **RESOLVED by #232 Amendment A** (below): company scope is now enforced on every policy command through the existing assignment scope.
3. **Revision without conversion.** CERT-FIN-02 §1 defines a later change as approval -> effective date -> impact assessment -> conversion -> activation. This foundation builds the approval, effective date and activation. Impact assessment and conversion remain unbuilt, and they must exist before any cost-engine consumer reads a revised policy.
4. **Activation has no separation of duties.** A principal holding prepare and activate can activate their own version after someone else approves it. #232 requires independence for approval only.
5. **Other Roles.** Should `accountingManager` prepare? Should `generalManager` read?
6. **Administrator by standing.** The Administrator's approve and activate come from standing (#223), with no grant. The alternative is an exclusion plus an explicit grant.

**Boundary.**
- No grant, Role or persona change.
- No nonprod or production data touched.
- No Firebase change.
- No UI (a later PR).

## #232 Amendment A — multi-company Controller and company-scoped financial authority (2026-10-13)

(Owner decision of 2026-10-13, amending #232. Resolves #232's open decision "company scope is data-only".)

**Decision (as directed by the Owner).**
1. One employee identity may hold Controller responsibilities for multiple operating companies.
2. Employee company assignments determine where role capabilities apply.
3. Controller permissions are evaluated against the requested operating company.
   - A Controller assigned to Taylor and Ventana may prepare and submit separate policies for each.
   - A Controller assigned only to Taylor is refused for Ventana.
4. Policies, cost histories and activation stay company-specific.
5. Authorized consolidated financial reporting is permitted; consolidated policy editing is not.
6. Owner / Administrator approval and activation stay subject to separation of duties.
7. No role may bypass company scope merely because it has a tenant-wide capability.
8. Reuse existing EOS structures; NO Financials-only company-access system.

**Implementation (PR #2085, unmerged).**
- **No new access system.** It reuses the existing Security Role ASSIGNMENT SCOPE: `user_role_assignments` scope type `operatingCompany`, whose governed values are this tenant's ACTIVE `tenant_operating_companies`. The Administration UI already assigns Roles with that scope.
- **Registry.** `SCOPE_EVALUABLE_GRANTS` (`functions/src/adminPolicy/assignmentScopeRuntime.ts`) registers `finance.policy.read`, `.prepare`, `.approve` and `.activate` at operatingCompany scope. Their consumers are the seven `/operations/finance` policy operations. This is the existing registry used as documented.
- **Enforcement, server-side on every policy command** (`functions/src/eosFinance/financialPolicy.ts`, the `CommercialWriteScope` pattern):
  - A key is held through the flat (global) set, or through the companies its UNCONDITIONED scoped holdings admit (`admittedScopeValues`). Otherwise the answer is `CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`.
  - The requested company is resolved first: ACTIVE, never CONSOLIDATED. It is then admitted against the holding BEFORE any version is read. Otherwise the answer is `OUTSIDE_OPERATING_COMPANY_SCOPE` (403), the same for a real and a non-existent version id, so no other company's versions or state leak.
  - **Out of scope == missing.** For a caller holding the key only at scope, an unknown company, an inactive company (including a scoped company later made inactive) and an ACTIVE out-of-scope company all get the SAME `OUTSIDE_OPERATING_COMPANY_SCOPE` (403), so a scoped holder cannot probe which companies exist. A flat holder keeps the precise `OPERATING_COMPANY_UNKNOWN` (400). CONSOLIDATED is refused for everyone with `CONSOLIDATED_NOT_A_COMPANY`.
  - Conditioned holdings admit nothing (fail closed).
- **Separation of duties** is unchanged and decided per version.
- **Consolidated.** Consolidated policy editing (and reading) is refused. Consolidated financial reporting reads (`readFinanceWorkspace` and the other Finance reads) are untouched.
- **Global assignments.** A GLOBAL assignment, and Protected Administrator standing, reach every company. This is the current EOS meaning of "All (Global)", recorded pending the Owner's confirmation (open item 2).
- **Administrator standing** reaches every company for `finance.policy.read`, `.approve` and `.activate`, and never for `.prepare` (EDIT is not implied). Open item 2(b)'s "exemption for Administrator standing" means exactly this reach.

**Open items (Owner decisions; nothing changed for them).**
1. **The finance Roles cannot be company-scoped today.** `controller`, `accountingManager`, `financeManager` and `owner` carry `audit.event.read` / `admin.*`, so Administration refuses them at operatingCompany scope (`SCOPE_AMBIGUOUS_ADMINISTRATION`). Options:
   - **A (recommended):** a dedicated policy-preparer Role (`finance.policy.read` + `.prepare`, no Administration capability), created and scoped through Administration. No code.
   - **B:** remove `audit.event.read` from `controller`; its 24 other capabilities would go inert at a scope.
   - **C:** an EOS-wide change to how Administration capabilities interact with scope.
2. **What a global assignment means.**
   - (a) All companies: the current EOS meaning, as implemented.
   - (b) A scoped holding is required: this would need an EOS-wide `scopeRequired` extension, plus exemptions for the Owner and for Administrator standing.
3. **Direct principal grants remain a tenant-wide path (NOT closed; blocked on a decision).** `grantObjectActionToPrincipal` refuses any scope on a direct grant, and an unconditioned direct exception lands in the flat set. So Administration can still give one principal `finance.policy.*` for every company.
   - The review asked to add the four keys to the existing `RESERVED_CAPABILITY_HOLDERS` list. That list is a Role ALLOW-list: `forbiddenPair` makes every unlisted Role a SYSTEM_INVARIANT, so `grantObjectActionToRole` would refuse the Option A dedicated Role, and the matrix would mark the Administrator's standing cells as forbidden.
   - Doing that would contradict this amendment's recommended path, so it was not done.
   - Options:
     - (i) Reserve to named Roles. The Owner names the Role keys (for example `financeManager`, `controller`, `owner` and the Option A Role); each new Role then needs a code change.
     - (ii) A Role-only rule ("no direct grant, any Role"). This needs a small new list in `grantObjectActionToPrincipal`, which is a new mechanism and needs Owner approval.
     - (iii) An Administration operating procedure: no direct grants of `finance.policy.*`.
   
   Until it is decided, the only intended tenant-wide paths are a GLOBAL Role assignment and Administrator standing.
4. **The financeAccounting persona discrepancy.** Its Principal holds both `accountingManager` and `controller` globally in nonprod. See `docs/financials/financial-policy-foundation-authority.md` §6.

**Boundary.**
- No Role, capability or grant change anywhere live. Test Roles exist in local test tenants only.
- No Firebase change.
- No UI.

## #232 Phase 1 — Financial Policy security corrections (Owner-approved limited implementation, 2026-10-13)

(Owner approval of 2026-10-13 for a **Financial-Policy-only** implementation. It is NOT an EOS-wide company-membership redesign and NOT a generalized role-scoping migration. The EOS-wide mandatory-company-assignment ruling is a separate future programme, not implemented here; for this feature a GLOBAL Role assignment still means all companies.)

**Decision (as approved by the Owner).**
1. **Roles unchanged.** The existing Controller, Finance Manager and Accounting Manager Roles stay UNCHANGED.
2. **Preparer Role.** A narrowly scoped **Financial Policy Preparer** Role holds ONLY `finance.policy.read` + `finance.policy.prepare`.
   - One employee prepares for Taylor, Ventana or both through EXISTING company-scoped Role assignments (Amendment A).
   - Future companies come through the existing governed registry.
   - Each company's policy, versions and activation history stay separate.
3. **Security requirements.**
   - Company scope is enforced server-side on every operation, and out-of-scope requests are refused (Amendment A).
   - DIRECT GRANTS CANNOT BYPASS company restrictions.
   - Whoever prepared, edited or submitted a version cannot approve, reject OR ACTIVATE it.
   - Owner and Administrator approval / activation authority is preserved, and so are tenant isolation, audit and the protected-Owner invariants.
   - No implicit permissions and no new grants.

**Implemented (PR #2085).**
- **Activation separation of duties (Amendment A open item / A6: RESOLVED).** `activateFinancialPolicy` refuses an activator who is the version's preparer, any content author or the submitter (`SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES`, 403).
  - A database CHECK, `financial_policy_activator_independent`, holds the same line, and its refusal maps to the same governed answer.
  - The approver may activate.
- **Approve and activate are reserved to the Owner Role.** They use the existing `RESERVED_CAPABILITY_HOLDERS` allow-list (Owner G7 mechanism), so:
  - `grantObjectActionToRole` refuses them for every other Role (`SYSTEM_INVARIANT`);
  - `grantObjectActionToPrincipal` refuses them as direct grants;
  - a Role keyed `owner` cannot be created as a custom Role.
- **The Administrator keeps read, approve and activate by STANDING; the reservation does not affect it.**
  - `protectedAdministratorImpliedKeys` and the runtime capability resolution never consult the reserved list. That is why trade-in approval had to be excluded from standing separately, through `PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR_EXCLUSIONS`.
  - Proven: the Administrator still approves and activates at runtime.
  - The Administration matrix shows the Administrator's read / approve / activate cells as held with source `PROTECTED_ADMINISTRATOR`, and prepare as not held.
  - The role-detail view additionally names the reservation ruling (`forbiddenBy`) on the approve / activate cells; this is a display artifact, and authority is unchanged.
- **Runtime reservation.** `approveFinancialPolicy`, `rejectFinancialPolicy` and `activateFinancialPolicy` also check the reservation at request time, through the same primitives as trade-in approval's `requireReservedHolder` (`qualifyingGlobalRoles` + `reservedCapabilityAdmits`; the Commercial command kernel itself may only be reached from the Commercial transport). A role-capability row that bypassed the write path does not authorize.
  - UNLIKE trade-in (excluded from standing), Protected Administrator standing also passes, because #232 gives the Administrator approve / activate by standing.
  - The refusal is `RESERVED_CAPABILITY` (403).
- **NULL-safe independence.** The CHECK `financial_policy_content_authors_no_null` (`array_position(content_authors, NULL) IS NULL`) stops a NULL author from blinding the three independence CHECKs.
- **Grants.** The Owner Role's approve / activate grants remain PROPOSED. Executing them needs the Owner's authorization through Administration.
- **Future companies (proven).** A third ACTIVE company in the registry is assignable at Preparer scope and keeps its own isolated policy and history, with no code change.

**The Preparer Role, and what remains open.**
- **Creating the Role needs no code.** Creating the Financial Policy Preparer Role needs only an Owner-authorized Administration action: a custom Role (`createRole`) granted exactly `finance.policy.read` + `.prepare` (`grantObjectActionToRole`), assigned globally or per company. The test tenant does exactly this (`financialPolicyPreparer`, alongside the unchanged finance Roles).
- **What is blocked** is closing DIRECT principal grants of read / prepare.
  - Reserving them through `RESERVED_CAPABILITY_HOLDERS` would make `createRole` refuse that Role key (the PR-4a guard against a custom Role impersonating a reserved holder).
  - No other existing mechanism refuses direct grants.
  - Until one of the options below is authorized, a direct principal grant of `finance.policy.read` / `.prepare` remains a tenant-wide path:
    - (A) a narrow `createRole` exception for this one Role key, then reserve read / prepare to it;
    - (C) a Role-only rule for read / prepare in `grantObjectActionToPrincipal`;
    - (B) a catalog edit: define the Role in the governed role catalog (`functions/src/access/governedBusinessRoles.ts`, the Firebase-era catalog the seed reads). This is Firebase-catalog development and a seed default, so it is listed for completeness only.

**Status of earlier open items.**
- **Amendment A item 1 (which Role carries scoped preparation).** DECIDED: the Financial Policy Preparer Role, created through Administration on the Owner's authorization; no code is needed.
- **Amendment A item 3 (direct grants).** RESOLVED for approve / activate (reserved). OPEN for read / prepare, as above.
- **Activation separation of duties.** RESOLVED.

**Remaining open items.**
1. Correcting a scheduled (future-dated) version.
2. `accountingManager` prepare and `generalManager` read.
3. The financeAccounting persona registry discrepancy.
4. Authorization of the Owner Role's approve / activate grants.
5. Authorize creating the Preparer Role through Administration.
6. Close direct grants of read / prepare: (A) or (C) above.

**Boundary.**
- No Role definition, grant, assignment or persona change anywhere live.
- No Firebase change.
- No UI.

### #232 Phase 1 — Option C: read / prepare are role-assignment-only (Owner-authorized, 2026-10-13)

(Owner authorization: a narrow restriction that admits only Role assignments for `finance.policy.read` and `finance.policy.prepare`. Direct principal grants are refused through governed Administration, INCLUDING at request time when a prohibited grant already exists. Role grants and the custom Financial Policy Preparer Role are preserved; no unrelated capability is affected.)

**Implementation (PR #2085).**
- **The list.** `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_ONLY_CAPABILITIES` (`functions/src/adminPolicy/roleCapabilityAdministration.ts`, beside `RESERVED_CAPABILITY_HOLDERS`) contains exactly `finance.policy.read` and `finance.policy.prepare`, each with its ruling. A test pins the list.
  - Unlike the reserved list, it names NO Role. Any Role may hold the keys, and `createRole` is unaffected.
- **Grant time.** `grantObjectActionToPrincipal` refuses these keys with `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_ONLY` (a CONFLICT, the same family as the reserved `SYSTEM_INVARIANT` refusal). No row is written.
  - The grant-impact preview runs the same command, so it reports `WOULD_REFUSE` / `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_ONLY`, never `WOULD_APPLY`.
- **Request time.** The hook is the resolver, so every OPERATIONAL gate, the explanation and the preview agree:
  - `resolveOperationalCapabilities`, the one resolution behind every runtime gate and `explainEffectiveAccess`, drops a direct exception for these keys, so a pre-existing row confers nothing flat or per-record, and never widens a company-scoped Role holding;
  - the Administration effective-access read (`resolvePrincipalEffectiveAccess`) drops it too;
  - the Workforce command kernel's direct-grant resolver (`withDirectCapabilityGrants`, `employeeAdministrationAuthority.ts`) drops it too.
  - The explanation therefore shows the key as not conferred (`directGrant: null`, result `DENIED`).
  - A Role assignment, global or company-scoped, still authorizes. So does Administrator standing, for read only.
- **Drift.** `verifyTenantAuthority` reports a stored prohibited direct row as `FORBIDDEN_PRINCIPAL_HOLDING`. This is a one-line, list-driven extension of the reserved-key census. Nothing is revoked automatically.
- **Preserved.**
  - Role grants of read / prepare, and creating a custom Preparer Role through Administration (tested).
  - Company-scope enforcement.
  - Separation of duties on approve, reject and activate.
  - The Owner reservation of approve / activate.
  - Administrator standing.

**Status.** Direct grants of read / prepare (Phase 1 open item 6, "B1") are RESOLVED. Open item 5 (authorize creating the Preparer Role through Administration) remains.

**Raw readers left UNFILTERED by design.** These are display-only or latent, and confer nothing:
- `capabilityKeysFor` (`administrationCapabilityGate.ts`). It gates Administration keys only, and is the source of the preview's `latent` / `adminKeys`.
- The `directGrants` echo in `resolvePrincipalEffectiveAccess`, which lists the stored rows.
- The grant matrix's `DIRECT_EXCEPTION enforced: true` display (below).

**Display (not changed).** The Administration grant matrix still lists a stored prohibited direct row as a `DIRECT_EXCEPTION` with `enforced: true`; only the runtime, the explanation and the effective-access read treat it as conferring nothing. Correcting that display is a later UI decision.

### #232 Phase 3 — withdraw / cancel lifecycle (2026-10-14)

(Owner requirement, from the Phase 3 nonprod finding: an APPROVED version held the company's single in-flight slot until activation, so approving without activating stranded the company, and an abandoned DRAFT or SUBMITTED version could not be removed from flight.)

**Decision (as required by the Owner).**
1. Authorized preparers may **withdraw their own** DRAFT or SUBMITTED versions, within their existing company scope.
2. The Owner and the Administrator may **cancel** an APPROVED version that is not yet activated.
3. Withdrawal and cancellation **preserve** the version, its decision history and its audit trail, and **release** the company's in-progress slot.
4. An ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED (already activated) version is **never** withdrawn or cancelled through this mechanism.
5. Separation of duties, company-scoped authorization and database-enforced race safety are preserved.

**Implemented (local; migration `1764570000000_financial-policy-withdraw-cancel.sql`).**
- **Two FINAL statuses.** `DRAFT | SUBMITTED -> WITHDRAWN` and `APPROVED -> CANCELLED`. Nothing leaves them, and ACTIVE / SUPERSEDED / REJECTED never enter them (transition trigger). Neither is ever in force (in force = ACTIVE / SUPERSEDED by date), and both fall outside the one-in-flight index, so the slot frees with no index change.
- **Stamps.** Write-once `withdrawn_by / withdrawn_at / withdrawal_reason` and `cancelled_by / cancelled_at / cancellation_reason`, held by the stamps-match-status CHECK. The reason has its own column, not `decision_reason`: on an APPROVED version that column already holds the approval note and is write-once with the approval.
- **No new capability, no grant.** `withdrawFinancialPolicy` reuses `finance.policy.prepare` (company-scoped, role-assignment-only); `cancelFinancialPolicy` reuses `finance.policy.approve` with its request-time Owner reservation (Administrator standing passes). Cancelling an approval is a decision act, so approve, not activate, governs it.
- **Ownership and independence, server and database.** The withdrawer must be a content author (the creator is the first) or the submitter: `NOT_YOUR_VERSION` (403), CHECK `financial_policy_withdrawer_owns_version`. The canceller must be neither the submitter nor a content author: `SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES` (403), CHECK `financial_policy_canceller_independent`. The approver may cancel their own approval.
- **Lifecycle refusals.** `FINANCIAL_POLICY_NOT_WITHDRAWABLE` / `FINANCIAL_POLICY_NOT_CANCELLABLE` (409); an ACTIVE or SUPERSEDED version answers `FINANCIAL_POLICY_LOCKED`. A reason is required (`REASON_REQUIRED`).
- **Concurrency.** Activation and cancellation take the same per-company advisory lock and the version's row lock, then re-read the status. Independently, the trigger admits ACTIVE and CANCELLED only from APPROVED, so whichever commits first wins and the other is a governed 409, never a 500.
- **Replay and audit.** An identical re-send answers `replayed: true`; a different reason is `FINANCIAL_POLICY_REPLAY_CONFLICT`. Each act writes one `finance.policy.withdraw` / `finance.policy.cancel` audit row with the full snapshot. `rebuildFinancialPolicyVersions` treats the new fields as null on snapshots written before the migration.
- **Screen.** Administration → Financial Policy offers Withdraw on the in-progress DRAFT / SUBMITTED version and Cancel Approval on an APPROVED one, each through a confirmation with a required reason; availability is the server's `yourActions` (`withdraw`, `cancel`), also listed per company by `readMyFinancialPolicyAuthority`.

**Not changed.** Roles, grants, assignments, capabilities, nonprod, production, Firebase, the training guide.

- **In order.** A transition writes only its own stamps; every other lifecycle stamp keeps its prior value, so a direct write cannot forge, say, a submission stamp on DRAFT → WITHDRAWN (independent-review finding, PR #2088).

**Owner rulings (2026-10-14, Financial Policy Closure) — applied.**
- **Withdrawal.** A policy author may withdraw their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED version while they retain the required company authorization: any content author (the creator or any editor) or the submitter, holding `finance.policy.prepare` at that company.
- **Cancellation.** An authorized approver may cancel an APPROVED version, **including their own approval**, with a mandatory reason and an audit event. Only the submitter and content authors are excluded.
- **Scheduled versions stay cancellable until activation actually occurs.** A version activated with a future effective date (ACTIVE, or already SUPERSEDED by a later activation) is SCHEDULED until that date; until then it may be cancelled exactly like an APPROVED one (`ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED -> CANCELLED`, server `cancelState` and the trigger, both on the company's business date). Its activation and supersession stamps are kept. The version it superseded at activation keeps governing: in force is resolved by date, and CANCELLED is never in force. This closes Phase 1 open item 1 (§6 item 7 of the authority document).
- **A version in force is never cancelled** (`FINANCIAL_POLICY_LOCKED`, server and trigger). Cancellation releases the in-progress slot; immutable history, separation of duties and the concurrency protections are unchanged.

### #232 company-access correction — company assignment is mandatory for Financial Policy (2026-10-14)

(Owner authorization 2026-10-14, applying the Owner ruling of 2026-10-13: business access requires BOTH a role capability AND an explicit operating-company assignment. Supersedes #232 Amendment A's "a GLOBAL assignment (or Administrator standing) reaches every company".)

**Rule (`functions/src/eosFinance/financialPolicy.ts`, `capabilityReach`).** A `finance.policy.*` action applies at operating company C only when the principal (1) holds the action's capability — flat (a global Role, e.g. the Owner Role; or standing) or through an unconditioned operatingCompany-scoped holding — and (2) has an explicit, active operatingCompany-scoped assignment for C: a C-scoped holding of that key, or, for a key held flat, a C-scoped holding of `finance.policy.read`. Lifecycle state, separation of duties, the Owner reservation on approve / activate and the audit behaviour are unchanged.
- A global holding or Administrator standing **alone reaches no company**. There is no implicit "all companies".
- The company assignment supplies **reach only, never a key**: a read-only assignment cannot become approval or activation, which stay reserved to the Owner Role / standing.
- An unknown or inactive company now answers `OUTSIDE_OPERATING_COMPANY_SCOPE` for every caller (formerly `OPERATING_COMPANY_UNKNOWN` for flat holders), so no caller learns whether an unassigned company exists.

**Administration shape (nonprod R1–R4, no code).** A custom Role `financialPolicyReviewer` holding exactly `finance.policy.read`, assigned to the Owner persona at `operatingCompany:taylor` and `operatingCompany:ventana`. No Administrator assignment: the Administrator loses Financial Policy business access. Finance Controller (Preparer @ Taylor) and Bai (Preparer @ Taylor + Ventana) are unchanged; their Preparer assignments are their company assignments.

**Order.** R1–R4 are applied before this code deploys; deployed first, the Owner would lose Financial Policy access until assigned (fail closed).

**Not changed.** The `finance.policy` navigation surface (earned by a flat or scoped read; the door confers nothing and the company selector lists only assigned companies), any other module, the EOS-wide company-membership model.

### Financials Workspace P0 correction — reachability and company-scoped authorization (2026-10-14)

(Owner direction 2026-10-14, applying the Owner ruling of 2026-10-13: business access requires BOTH a capability AND an explicit operating-company assignment. Finding from the Financials employee acceptance at 328c75c3: the PostgreSQL Finance workspace was unreachable for every persona, and every `finance.payment.read` holder read Taylor, Ventana and Consolidated.)

**Rule (`functions/src/eosFinance/financeCompanyAccess.ts`).** A finance key applies at operating company C only with the key (flat, or company-scoped) AND an explicit, active operatingCompany-scoped assignment for C: a C-scoped holding of that key, or — for a key held flat — of `finance.payment.read` (the Finance view key), now registered in `SCOPE_EVALUABLE_GRANTS`. The same rule as Financial Policy (#2089).
- A global Role (controller, accountingManager, generalManager, owner) or Administrator standing **alone reaches no company**.
- The assignment confers **reach, never a key**: settlement / reconciliation still need their own keys.
- **Consolidated** only when every active company is reached.
- **Out of scope == unknown**: an unassigned, unknown or inactive company gets the same refusal (`OUTSIDE_OPERATING_COMPANY_SCOPE`); a record of an unassigned company answers like a missing one (`OBLIGATION_NOT_FOUND`, `SETTLEMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `APPLICATION_NOT_FOUND`).

**Applied to.** Every `/operations/finance` read (workspace, obligations, settlements, drill-through) and settlement command (record, apply — including each applied obligation, reverse, void, reconcile); the new read `readMyFinanceCompanyAccess` (the workspace's company selector); every Analysis measure read only through `finance.*` keys (refused, with its exceptions withheld, unless the caller is assigned to every company in scope). PostgreSQL Finance business logic is unchanged. Non-finance Analysis measures, cost evidence supply and intercompany relief (warehouse-scoped) are unchanged.

**Reachability.** The Financials Overview (which hosts the workspace) earns the `financials.payments` surface — the surface earned by the workspace's own key. Its legacy placeholder row STAYS, so the legacy navigation source (production) is byte-identical; the row changes kind from ungoverned to cutover — the `purchasing/suppliers` and `administration/financialPolicy` precedent — with ceilings cutover 22 → 23 and ungoverned 40 → 39, total unchanged at 62. **This ceiling move is recorded for Owner confirmation.**

**Scoped-only holders.** A principal holding `finance.payment.read` only through a company-scoped assignment reads Finance and Analysis finance measures at that company; the `financials.payments` / `analysis.workspace` navigation doors remain flat-earned (the surface catalog admits a scoped door only on a list read), so such a principal has no menu entry. No such principal exists or is proposed.

**Governance (proposed, NOT executed).** A `financeCompanyAccess` Role holding exactly `finance.payment.read`, assigned per company. Until assigned, every Finance user is refused (fail closed): the assignments must be applied before this deploys.

## #233 — OWNER: O-0 repository privacy is DEFERRED to the final delivery stage (2026-10-15)

**Status: DEFERRED — OWNER DIRECTED.**

**Decision.**
1. Do not change the visibility of `TaylorService-spec/Taylor_Parts` now. Repository privacy (O-0 in the EOS product program plan, `docs/architecture/eos-product-program.md` §3) is revisited as a **final commercial-release readiness item**.
2. O-0 is **not** a dependency or blocker for:
   - the Firebase exit (O-1);
   - EOS Core authority;
   - the customer deployment architecture (O-9);
   - the UX redesign;
   - employee UAT;
   - nonproduction development.

   All previously authorized work continues.
3. Strict protections stay in force while the repository is public:
   - **Never commit** credentials, customer information or sensitive evidence.
   - The existing secret-scanning and repository security controls stay active, including the `gitleaks` check on pull requests and the Firebase exit and equivalence guards.
   - Sensitive local evidence stays outside git: the 2026-10-14 cleanup evidence is local only, credentials are in Keeper, and production and migration evidence is in the encrypted restricted-Drive archive.
4. **Do not reopen this decision** unless a verified security exposure requires immediate action.

**Context.**
- The SaaS readiness assessment (PR #2054, OD-2) and the product program plan both recommended making the repository private. The Owner has sequenced that to the end of delivery.
- A 2026-10-14 review classified the committed `executionModeToken` (`functions/authpr4/production-authorization.json`) as a non-secret execution marker; there is no exposure that requires reopening.

## #234 — OWNER: Firebase exit, EOS Core authority, customer deployment model, and the D-1 / D-2 scoping (2026-10-15)

**Status: DECIDED (O-1, O-2, O-9). AUTHORIZED WITH GATES (D-1, D-2).** These are established architectural decisions; do not treat them as open.

**O-1 — Zero Firebase dependency: CONFIRMED target.**
- EOS eliminates every Firebase dependency: authentication, navigation, business data, security rules and application access.
- This supersedes the "IDENTITY_ONLY" end state recorded for FX-AUTH-001 in `firebase-exit-ratchet.md` and `firebase-exit-baseline.json`.
- **Authorized:** read-only inventory, dependency analysis, migration design, and preparation of incremental implementation PRs.
- **Not authorized:** identity or data cutovers. Each needs its required proof and a separate Owner authorization.

**O-2 — EOS Core authority: CONFIRMED (correction of the product plan's earlier "domain model" wording).**
- EOS Core owns the domain model **and all governed business authority**, enforced server-side:
  - business entities and relationships;
  - identity and the Employee association;
  - effective permissions and authorization;
  - record ownership, accountability and assignment;
  - company and tenant boundaries;
  - workflows, business rules and approvals;
  - business data access;
  - auditability and administrative configuration.
- **Frontend navigation is not an authorization boundary.**
- The plan's former O-2 (product domain / `app.` + `api.` hostnames) is renumbered **O-15** and remains open.

**O-9 — Customer deployment model: CONFIRMED.**
- A shared product codebase with dedicated customer deployments and governed customer/company isolation.
- Taylor Freezer of Arizona and Ventana keep their distinct operating-company boundaries.

**D-1 — Equipment import: AUTHORIZED to investigate and prepare a fail-closed guard.**
- No writes to the Firebase (Firestore) equipment store are permitted.
- Activating anything that affects live imports requires regression proof.

**D-2 — Finance grants: AUTHORIZED for read-only examination only.**
- Examine actual effective grants, historical provenance and intended role/company scope.
- No revocation, expansion or change of Finance grants without the exact change set presented for Owner approval.

**Still separately gated:** identity migration, permission/grant changes, financial grants, production deployment and destructive migrations. O-0 remains DEFERRED (#233).

## #235 — OWNER: EOS Core Company Authority V1 — Analysis and My Work company isolation (2026-10-15)

**Status: OWNER APPROVED (security ruling, 2026-10-15).** Applied to Analysis and My Work only. These need separate decisions: Commercial reads, the `/operations/rental` reads and site search (`searchEos`).

**Why.** Lane D's authenticated UAT of #2099 at `a1261486` found that Analysis and My Work Key figures defaulted to a consolidated view of **every active company**, whatever the caller's assignment. `eosAnalysis/analysis.ts` `companyScope` took no actor. As a result, real Ventana figures reached Taylor-only office, retail and national-accounts staff. #2099 is merged and deployed, with security acceptance OPEN until this correction passes authenticated runtime tests.

**Rule (`functions/src/eosOps/companyAuthority.ts` `resolveCompanyAuthority(db, tenantId, principalId)`).** EOS Core owns company authority. It is server-side and read-only, and grants nothing.
1. **Identity.** An ENABLED Principal with an ACTIVE tenant membership and EXACTLY ONE active Employee link, to an access-eligible Employee (ACTIVE / CONTRACTOR).
   - No link, more than one link, or a missing or ineligible Employee means **no authority**. Identity ambiguity fails closed.
2. **Ordinary authority.** That Employee's home operating company (`eos_workforce.employees.operating_company_id`), when it is ACTIVE for the tenant.
3. **Explicit expansion (Owner Q1).** Every company named by the Principal's ACTIVE, non-stale, tenant-matching `operatingCompany`-scoped role assignments, when that company is ACTIVE.
   - This confers REACH only, never a capability.
4. **Never.**
   - A global Role, Administrator standing, a Firebase claim, or a frontend or client-selected company implies no company.
   - No role-name exceptions.
5. **Result.** The union of 2 and 3. Empty means no company data.

**Applied to (Owner Q2).**
- `readAnalysisWorkspace` and `readMeasureAnalysis`, and through them My Work's attention, insights, Key figures and the Analysis rental exceptions.
- **My Work's `rental` section.**
