**Not done, deliberately.** No Firebase code removed; no production change; no new read key.

## #G-1b (number assigned at merge) — Goals: what governs a date, SCHEDULED versions, and corrective replacement (G-1b, resolves F1 and F3 and the F2 decision from the G-1 live acceptance, 2026-10-20)

**Evidence:** the G-1 live acceptance on nonprod (`evidence/g1-goal-authoring-live-acceptance-2026-10-20.md`, findings F1, F2, F3). **Owner decision (option A, relayed 2026-10-20):** "An approved future-dated replacement that has not yet taken effect may NOT be retired. Goal-version history is immutable. A closed date window is never reopened or extended." EOS only: **no Firebase code or rules changed**; `functions/src/performance/*` is untouched (the Firebase `currentGoalFor` still selects APPROVED only; the Firebase exit replaces it).

**F1 — a SUPERSEDED version stopped governing the dates its window still covers.** Approving a future-dated successor marks the predecessor SUPERSEDED at once (window closed the day before the successor starts), and the read selected `status = 'APPROVED'` only — so from approval until the successor's start no target was in force, and every historical as-of read of a superseded or retired period returned "no goal". **The governed fix (EOS selection, `eosOps/performanceGoalReads.ts` `governingGoalFor`):** the version in force on a date is the one that carries **approval evidence** (status APPROVED, or SUPERSEDED / RETIRED with an approver) and whose window covers the date. A DRAFT, and a discarded draft (RETIRED, no approver), never govern. A RETIRED-after-approval version governs the days before its close. **Ambiguity is still a refusal** (`GOAL_AMBIGUOUS`, rendered UNAVAILABLE, never "no goal", never the newer one). The window and closing math, the supersede transaction and the schema are unchanged (no migration). The same predicate (`governingVersions`) now drives the authoring overlap checks (create-first-version and approve), so a window that was governed cannot be claimed again while a read would call it ambiguous.

**Consumers examined.** (1) `listCurrentPerformanceGoals` (EOS read) — the only EOS selection; switched to `governingGoalFor`. (2) The dashboard goal tiles (`goalProgress`, `usePerformanceGoals`) consume that read's `goal` and its target/direction only; they do not test `status`, so a governing SUPERSEDED/RETIRED version is compared like any other, for the dates its window covers. (3) `performanceGoalAuthoring.ts` overlap checks (create ~L269, approve clash) — moved to the governing predicate. (4) Firebase `comparePlanToActual` (FIN-003: refuses anything not APPROVED) and the Firebase callables — out of scope by the Owner's correction (we are replacing Firebase, not fixing it); recorded, not changed. Nothing made the answer non-unique, so no STOP.

**F3 + Owner points 2–3 — SCHEDULED.** An APPROVED version whose start is after today shows **Scheduled** (today = the screen's existing UTC date source, the same clock the commands use), never "In force". A SUPERSEDED version whose window still covers today reads "In force until <date>"; one that was replaced before it started reads "Replaced before it started".

**F2 — retiring a SCHEDULED version is refused (Owner option A).** `retirePerformanceGoal` on an APPROVED version with `effectiveFrom > today` → `GOAL_SCHEDULED_NOT_RETIRABLE` (PRECONDITION_FAILED), "This target hasn't started yet, so it can't be retired. To change it, set a corrective replacement for someone else to approve." No mutation, no command record, no audit row. The screen hides **Retire** on a SCHEDULED row and offers **Replace**. (The retire path's "close at its own start" branch is therefore dead and removed; a retire always closes at today.) A started version is retired exactly as before.

**Corrective replacement of a SCHEDULED version (Owner points 4–8).** A draft whose `supersedesGoalId` is a SCHEDULED version needs `.supersede` and the same two-person, self-target, reach, company-isolation and idempotency rules as any replacement (the same `decideWrite`). On approval, in ONE transaction: (a) the SCHEDULED version becomes SUPERSEDED — **its row, window and audit are kept untouched**; (b) the **preceding** version (the one the scheduled version replaced) has its end moved to the day before the corrected start, earlier or later; (c) the draft becomes APPROVED; the overlap check then runs against the corrected windows. **Representation of "never governed" (no schema change, no window rewrite):** the table's window CHECK (`effective_to >= effective_from`) cannot express "superseded before its start", so it is **derived**: a SUPERSEDED version whose approved successor was approved on a UTC day **before the version's own start** never governed (`neverGoverned`; mirrored by the screen). A version replaced on or after its start day governed its window, as before. Result: exactly one governing version per date, no overlap, no gap — proven on the boundary dates (start-1, start, start+1) for an earlier, the same and a later corrected start.

**Controller interpretation (verbatim from the Owner decision file; reconciles point 7 with "never extend a closed window"):**
- "Closed" and "historical" mean dates that have already elapsed (before today, on the authoring clock).
- A boundary set by a SCHEDULED (not-yet-effective) successor is a scheduled transition, not history.
- An approved corrective version may move that boundary to its own start, earlier or later.
- No elapsed date's governing version ever changes.
- A SCHEDULED version that is superseded before it takes effect is recorded as never having governed. It stays on record and governs no date.

**Choices made under that interpretation (logged).** (1) **A corrected start must be after today — refused, not clamped** (`GOAL_START_ELAPSED`, INVALID_INPUT), checked when the draft is written AND when it is approved (a draft that was valid when written can have become elapsed by approval). A clamp would answer with a start date nobody typed, and an elapsed start would either govern a day that has already passed or move an elapsed boundary. (2) The preceding boundary moves only if the scheduled version set it (it equals the day before the scheduled start); a window that ended earlier on its own is only ever shortened, never lengthened. (3) Once the scheduled version has **started** (`effectiveFrom <= today`) a replacement is an ordinary supersede (it governed its elapsed days; the successor starts after it began) — the corrective path applies only while the version is still scheduled. (4) A correction of a scheduled version with no preceding version (a first version) moves nothing; it only requires the corrected start to be after today. (5) **A correction of a correction.** The version whose end moves is the one that GOVERNS until the scheduled start, found by walking `supersedesGoalId` back past every version that never governed (`precedingOf`); the draft's start guard and the boundary move both use it, and **no never-governed row's window is ever written**. Governing is decided over ALL of the target's versions (a never-governed version's successor must be in view), then the draft and the version it replaces are set aside for the overlap check. Proven for a second correction starting earlier than both, at the first correction's start, between the two, at the original scheduled start, and later than both, with exactly one governing version on every day of the year. (6) **One clock per approval.** The correction-versus-ordinary branch and the approval timestamp that `neverGoverned` reads come from the same instant, so they agree across midnight UTC. Approving on the day BEFORE the scheduled start is a correction (the scheduled version never governed); approving ON its start day is an ordinary supersede (it governed that day). "Today" is the UTC date (after 5 pm Arizona time it is already tomorrow there; the date hint on the screen shows it). (7) **A scheduled FIRST version (no predecessor) can never be withdrawn, only replaced** — under Option A a scheduled version is not retirable and nothing precedes it, so until its start the only change is a corrective replacement someone else approves; this is the Owner's decision and is recorded here for visibility, not worked around.

**Known data note (nonprod live acceptance rows).** The G-1 live walk retired a not-yet-started version (GB, window 11-01..11-01). Under the new rule it governs that one day (RETIRED after approval), and the dates after it have no target — it is test data, now unreachable by a new action, and is not rewritten.

**Pins moved with it.** None of the governed counts (no migration, no capability, no Operation). New tests are in the existing registered files: `g1GoalAuthoring.test.mjs` (offline), `g1GoalAuthoringPostgres.test.mjs` (Postgres), `performanceGoalsScreen.test.jsx` (screen).

**Not done, deliberately.** No Firebase change (`comparePlanToActual`, the callables); no production action; no migration; no change to the window/closing math or the supersede transaction.

## #Q-1a (number assigned at merge) — Every applied Commercial and CRM command writes ONE audit row (Q-1 PR 1, B5 stage 6, 2026-10-20)

**Gap (B5 acceptance matrix, stage 6, FAIL).** Commercial and CRM commands kept an idempotency receipt and nothing else: no `eos_policy.audit_events` row said who changed an Opportunity, an Agreement, a trade-in value, a discount, a Sales Order, a customer or a site, or what it was before. The one exception was CRM activity (F7b).

**The one governed answer (no Owner input needed).** The EOS convention of `cycleCountOperations.ts` and `performanceGoalAuthoring.ts`: ONE row per APPLIED command, in the command's own transaction — `action` is the operation, `actor_uid` the Principal, `target_kind` / `target_id` the record, `before` / `after` structured fields (before null for a create; only the changed fields for an edit), the reason where the command takes one. A replay returns before the command body and writes nothing; a refusal rolls back and writes nothing; if the audit write itself fails the whole command fails (no applied-but-unaudited command). The raw idempotency key is never stored. `after` carries the protected-Administrator provenance stamp like every other direct writer.

**The content rule (review round, controller).** `audit_events` is append-only by trigger, so whatever lands there can never be erased: **audit rows carry identity, state and amounts, never free text or contact details; free text is recorded as a length or a changed flag.** Kept: ids, numbers, statuses, amounts, quantities, part and line ids, the customer PO number (`customerPO`, an identifier the customer issued, like an order number), the names that identify an account, contact or site, and the governed reasons. Recorded as a length (`<field>Length`, plus a `<field>Changed` flag on an edit): Opportunity `need` and `nextAction`, Agreement `shippingInstructions`, `specialInstructions` and `shipVia`, Contact `contactRole`, a line's `warranty`, a trade-in `description`, Account `notes`, site `accessNotes`. Recorded as presence or a changed flag: contact email and phone, the Account billing address, the site street address, Account tags (a count). Same precedent as `crmActivityAuthority` (`bodyLength`, never the body). Also in the round: the Agreement `updateDraft` audit states the charges AFTER `syncApprovedTradeInCredit`, and `create` / `updateDraft` record each trade-in's proposed value, status and decision; every string is made well-formed (a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD) before the jsonb write; the trade-in decision and the service-provider authorize / revoke reasons take the existing Commercial 500-character reason limit (`MAX_HANDOFF_REASON_LENGTH`; the handoff reason already carried it, and the CRM Account handoff reason has its own 500), refused `REASON_TOO_LONG`; the service-provider revoke audit names `serviceOperatingCompanyKey`.

**Inventory (22 commands; the PR body lists them).** Commercial, 14, through `runCommercialCommand`, whose outcome now REQUIRES an `audit` (a new command cannot compile without stating one; the kernel writes it before the receipt): `opportunity.create / update / transition / closeAsWon`; `salesAgreement.create / updateDraft / accept / approveTradeIn / declineTradeIn` (the customer discount rides create and updateDraft; the trade-in decision carries its reason); `salesOrder.create / createFromOpportunity / transition / authorizeServiceProvider / revokeServiceProvider`. CRM, 8: `crm.createAccount / updateAccount` (an owner handoff's reason is the audit reason), `crm.createContact / updateContact / importAccountContacts` (ONE row for the whole import, naming the Account and every Contact it created), `crm.createAccountLocation / updateAccountLocation`; `crm.activity.create` already audited (unchanged).

**Not covered, deliberately.** Reads; the Firebase-era `accountImportCommand` (Firestore, its own audit event) and the one-off `commercial.c5.copy` / `crm.cutover.copy` migration copies (already audited); the Commercial fulfilment authority (already audits). No new capability, no grant, no migration, no Firebase change, no production action. Quote and discount APPROVAL is Q-1 PR 2 (a specification with Owner decisions); nothing of it is built here.

**Pins.** No governed count moves. Tests: `q1CommandAuditInventory.test.mjs` (offline: the served operation sets equal the audited inventory; the kernel writes the audit inside the transaction, before the receipt, after the body) and `q1CommercialCrmAuditPostgres.test.mjs` (Postgres: one row per applied command with the stated fields, none on replay or refusal, rollback with the command).

## #S1b (number assigned at merge) — Hard stock reservations per company AND warehouse (S1b, 2026-10-20)

**Authority.** Owner register 2026-10-20 section 1 S1a OD-2 and section 4 S1a tests; DECISIONS #165 (rulings 1, 2, 4 preserved); the S1a spec (PR #2167). Where the spec recommended a location-less pool (OD-2 A), the Owner ruled it NOT adopted: a hard reservation states an explicit operatingCompanyId AND a warehouse.

**What exists.** One commitment pool (`eos_ops.inventory_commitments`), arithmetic `RESERVED - RELEASED - CONSUMED` per (company, warehouse, Part), one function for the gate and the read. Company and warehouse are both STATED and must agree (command refusal COMPANY_WAREHOUSE_MISMATCH plus a composite foreign key to `warehouses`); the demand document must belong to the stated company (DEMAND_COMPANY_MISMATCH). A Sales Order claim is a row in the same ledger (nullable `work_order_id`, `sales_order_id` + `sales_order_line_number`, a CHECK for exactly one source; S1a OD-9 A). No oversell: the per-Part `lockStockLocation` lock, in sorted order, is taken before on-hand is read; a mutation that removes it fails the concurrency proof. Replay: derived row key + content fingerprint (same = replay, different = IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT), decided before the gate; one active claim per (demand line, Part, warehouse) (DUPLICATE_CLAIM). Governed transitions release / consume / cancel are bounded by the outstanding claim at that company and warehouse; one `stock.*` audit row per applied command, the reason its only free text; the table is append-only by trigger. Refusal vocabulary UNKNOWN_STOCK / INSUFFICIENT_STOCK before any write (S1a OD-7).

**What a reader sees.** `readPartBalance`: `reserved` is `NOT_YET_ACTIVATED` until the company is activated (`eos_ops.stock_reservation_activation`, an operator-inserted row per environment; S1a OD-4 A) and then a known number; headline `reserved` / `available` are `SCOPE_PARTIAL` when the Part is also stocked or claimed in an ACTIVE warehouse of a reachable company outside the caller's scope (nothing else about it is disclosed); `byLocation` carries exact per-warehouse reserved and available for in-scope warehouses. Unallocated demand (plans, order quantities) is never a hard reservation.

**Serial custody (settled, not designed).** A quantity row cannot name units, so a serialized or whole-unit Part is refused TRACKING_MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED before any write, for either demand source. A unit is therefore never claimed by this ledger, so it cannot be claimed twice. Claiming a NAMED unit on `serialized_custody` needs a custody holder that table lacks; that remains deferred (S1a OD-8, class C).

**Not built, deliberately.** (1) Dispatch wiring: neither demand family selects a warehouse and no warehouse-selection rule is ratified, so the Work Order edges do not call these commands yet; they take the warehouse explicitly. (2) The Sales Order allocation command, its screen and the `salesOrder.fulfill` / `.service` grants (S1c). (3) The Sales-Order-to-Work-Order hand-over (S1a OD-10). (4) Any new capability or grant: reserve, release and consume are system effects.

**Migration.** `1764710000000_stock-reservation-company-warehouse` (controller-authored): refuses to run if `inventory_commitments` holds rows (every existing row is an unlocated reservation; none is backfilled). Until it lands in `functions/migrations`, the suites that touch commitments apply the SQL from `functions/test/support/pendingMigrations/` (`stockReservationMigration.mjs`; a no-op once the real file exists, then delete the `.txt`).

**Operator runbook.** Activation per company and environment is one row: `INSERT INTO eos_ops.stock_reservation_activation (tenant_id, operating_company_key, activated_by) VALUES (...)`. Nonprod first; production is a separate operator action and Owner gate. With no row the command refuses RESERVATION_NOT_ACTIVATED and the read says NOT_YET_ACTIVATED.

**Tests.** `stockReservationPostgres.test.mjs` (the S1a section 4 list plus serial custody; the lock-removal mutant fails it), `eosOpsInventoryCommitment(Postgres).test.mjs`, `partBalancePostgres.test.mjs` (per-location reserved / available, SCOPE_PARTIAL, NOT_YET_ACTIVATED), and the SCN-4 reservation row of `scannerScenariosOnEosPostgres.test.mjs` (was a TODO blocked by lane RES).
